identity.name: Principality of Serbia
alt_names: Serbian principality of the Vlastimirovic dynasty

land.text: the Serbian principality: 'annexed by the Byzantine Empire (c. 970)' / 'in c. 969-971', the Catepanate of Ras c. 971; the infobox says 960

successors.note: The main page's infobox gives the Byzantine annexation as 960 but the body as c. 969-971; the Catepanate of Ras page: c. 971 under John Tzimiskes, 'territorial jurisdiction can not be precisely determined', disestablished 976. Bulgaria (the Cometopuli) held the region 976-1018.

capitals.name: Destinikon (site unidentified; Ras region)
capitals.note: 'The capital according to T. Zivkovic was likely Destinikon' (infobox). The page does not locate it; the point is the gazetteer's Stari Ras, the border stronghold of the Raska region, as a placeholder. During the Bulgarian annexation 924-933 there was no Serbian court. Reviewer eu-18-b: point moved to the Stari Ras page's coordinates (43°7′42″N 20°24′56″E, 'some 10-11 kilometers west of modern-day Novi Pazar'); the gazetteer's 20.6E lay east of every shape's bbox.

rulers.name: Vlastimir
rulers.title: archon
rulers.note: Succeeded Prosigoj c. 830 (main page); died c. 851 (Vlastimir page: 845-850 Runciman, 851 at the latest Zivkovic). Visheslav (from c. 780) and Radoslav and Prosigoj before him are not dated.

rulers.name: Mutimir
rulers.title: prince
rulers.note: With his brothers Strojimir and Gojnik as co-rulers to the 880s; the main page: 'Mutimir ruled until 890, being succeeded by his son Prvoslav' (Prvoslav's reign is not dated).

rulers.name: Petar Gojnikovic
rulers.title: prince
rulers.note: 'Petar Gojnikovic (r. 892-917)'; deposed by Simeon of Bulgaria in 917 and died in a Bulgarian dungeon (Simeon page).

rulers.name: Pavle Branovic
rulers.title: prince (Bulgarian nominee)
rulers.note: Placed on the throne by Simeon after 917; ousted by Zaharije, sent by the Byzantines 'in 920'.

rulers.name: Zaharije Prvoslavljevic
rulers.title: prince (Byzantine nominee)
rulers.note: Fled to Croatia when Caslav's Bulgarian army came in 924 (Simeon page).

rulers.name: Caslav Klonimirovic
rulers.title: prince
rulers.note: The page dates the start 'around 933/934' (scholars 927-934) and his death 943/960, with 960 favoured by Corovic and Fine; the Magyars captured and drowned him in the Sava.

correction.text: the early Serbian principality, held for 780-849

keyframe_review.note: 24.3 thousand km2 for 768-849. The main page's infobox has the principality 'established 780' ('its first ruler known by name was Viseslav, who started ruling around 780') and says 'the exact borders of the early Serbian state are unclear'; Vlastimir (c. 830) 'united the nearby Serbian tribes' (Vlastimir page). Corrected: the same outline for 780-849 (Cliopatria starts twelve years early). No infobox area.

36.3 thousand km2: +12 thousand. The Vlastimir page says that after 842 he 'expanded west, taking Bosnia and Herzegovina (Hum, also called Zahumlje)', sources disagreeing on the boundaries; the shape agrees in kind, the year is Cliopatria's (the page says 'after 842', Vlastimir died c. 851). The main page: 'the exact borders ... are unclear'.

37.8 thousand km2 under Mutimir (to 890) and Petar Gojnikovic (892-917). The only territorial statement dated in this span is the 853-854 repulse of Boris I's Bulgars (Vlastimir page); no border change. Kept.

37.0 thousand km2 for 911-921. The main page puts Petar's expansion 'north and west', the annexation of the Bosna valley and the Narentines' allegiance inside his reign (892-917) but gives no year; Cliopatria draws the larger shape from 922. The 917 deposition by Simeon and the Bulgarian and Byzantine nominees (Pavle Branovic 917-920, Zaharije from 920) are handled by the ledger's contest.

correction.text: the principality with the Bosna valley, held for 922-923

keyframe_review.note: 61.3 thousand km2 for 922-925. Simeon's commanders annexed Serbia in 924: 'Caslav ... was sent to depose Zaharije, who fled to Croatia ... Bulgaria annexed Serbia directly'; the main page: 'annexed in 924 by Simeon I and subjected to Bulgarian rule until 933'. Corrected: the same outline for 922-923; there is no Serbian state in 924-932 (the Bulgarian Cliopatria row covers the land from 926).

correction.text: Caslav's restored Serbia, as Cliopatria draws it from 936

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 933-935: Caslav 'secured the allegiance of the Dalmatian duchies and ended Bulgarian rule in central Serbia' (main page); his reign begins 'around 933/934' (Caslav page; scholars give 927-934). Cliopatria restores Serbia only in 936. Whether he held Bosnia is disputed (Dvornik c. 949; Novakovic and Zivkovic doubt it); the DAI counts the Bosna chorion in Serbia.

61.0 thousand km2 for 936-959. The Caslav page finds no evidence for Rascia, Travunia, Pagania or the Kanalites being added and says the DAI (c. 959) lists them as separate from Serbia, while Bosnia is the contested addition; the shape includes Bosnia. Kept with that caveat.
A one-year 61.0 thousand km2 shape for 960, the infobox year of the Byzantine annexation and the page's preferred time of Caslav's death. Kept as the last shape.

correction.text: the principality's last shape (960) is the one to use; the 961 sliver is dropped

keyframe_review.note: A 403 km2 sliver on the Bosnia-Croatia border (18.14-18.38E, 42.56-42.82N) for 961: no page describes a state of this size; the principality had fallen by 960 (infobox) or c. 969-971 (body). Drop it; the 960 shape is the last.

ledger.note: 780: the Serbian principality begins with Viseslav. 'Its first ruler known by name was Viseslav, who started ruling around 780'; infobox 'Established 780'. Cliopatria starts its shape in 768.

c. 850: Vlastimir takes Bosnia and Hum. 'After 842 ... expanded west, taking Bosnia and Herzegovina (Hum, also called Zahumlje)'; the page gives no year and says its sources disagree on the boundaries. The year is Cliopatria's shape change (850).

region.text: Serbia under Bulgarian and Byzantine nominees 917-924

ledger.note: 917: Simeon of Bulgaria attacks Serbia and deposes Petar. 'Symeon attacked Serbia (in 917) and deposed Peter, placing Pavle Branovic ... as Prince of Serbia'; the Byzantines send Zaharije to oust Pavle in 920.

minus.text: Cliopatria's Principality of Serbia shape of 922
Cliopatria's Principality of Serbia shape of 921

region.text: the Bosna valley and the north and west added to the 921 shape

ledger.note: 922: page silent on the year. Petar's expansion 'north and west', the annexation of 'the Bosna River valley' and the Narentines' allegiance belong to his reign (892-917), but Cliopatria draws the larger 61.3 thousand km2 shape (+24 thousand) only from 922.

region.text: Serbia under Bulgarian and Byzantine nominees 917-924

ledger.note: 924: Bulgaria annexes Serbia. Caslav is sent to depose Zaharije, who flees to Croatia; the Serbian nobles are beheaded and 'Bulgaria annexed Serbia directly' (Simeon page); 'annexed in 924 by Simeon I and subjected to Bulgarian rule until 933' (main page).
924: the whole principality passes to Bulgaria. 'Bulgaria annexed Serbia directly.'

c. 933: Caslav ends Bulgarian rule in Serbia. 'Caslav Klonimirovic (933- c. 943/960) led Serb refugees back to Serbia'; he 'ended Bulgarian rule in central Serbia'. Scholars date the start from 927 to 933/934 (Caslav page: 'around 933/934').

region.text: the Dalmatian duchies: Zahumlje, Travunia and the Narentines

ledger.note: c. 933: Caslav wins the allegiance of the Dalmatian duchies. He 'secured the allegiance of the Dalmatian duchies'; but the Caslav page finds no evidence that Zahumlje, Travunia or Pagania were added to the realm, and the DAI lists them as separate.

region.text: the Dalmatian duchies: Zahumlje, Travunia and the Narentines

ledger.note: 960: the allegiance lapses with Caslav's fall. Page silent on how long the Dalmatian duchies stayed attached; closed at the principality's end.

960: the principality falls. Infobox: Byzantine annexation 960; Caslav drowned by the Magyars c. 943/960 (Caslav page: 'around 960' favoured); the body dates the annexation c. 969-971 and the Catepanate of Ras to c. 971.

wars.name: Bulgarian invasion of Serbia under Presian
wars.outcome: Vlastimir 'resisted and defeated the Bulgarian army in a three-year-war'; the Bulgarian army 'devastated and driven out'.
wars.note: The Vlastimir page gives the invader as Presian I.

wars.name: Bulgarian invasion of Serbia under Boris I
wars.outcome: Vlastimir's sons repel Boris I and capture twelve boyars and his son Vladimir; peace follows.
wars.note: The main page dates the victory c. 853-854.

wars.name: Bulgarian-Serbian war (Simeon's conquest of Serbia)
wars.outcome: Simeon deposes Petar (917), puts Pavle Branovic on the throne, then Zaharije revolts for the Byzantines; in 924 Bulgaria annexes Serbia directly.
wars.note: Simeon page: Pavle, Zaharije and Petar's capture are undated; the main page dates 917, 920 and 924.

wars.name: Magyar invasion of Bosnia (Kisa)

zones.text: Bosnia, invaded by the Magyars under Kisa

wars.outcome: Caslav's voivode Tihomir kills Kisa at the Drina; Kisa's widow returns, surprises Caslav in Syrmia and drowns him in the Sava; the coalition of Serb principalities disintegrates.

certainty.note: 'The exact borders of the early Serbian state are unclear' (main page); the principality was 'a confederacy of Slavic principalities' under Caslav, and Bosnia, Zahumlje and Travunia are disputed throughout.

notes: Page budget (5) spent on the main article, Caslav, Vlastimir, Simeon I and the Catepanate of Ras; Petar Gojnikovic's own page could not be opened (Petar_Gojnikovic, Peter_Gojnikovic and the percent-encoded form all returned url_not_found), so the dating of his Bosna-valley and Narentine gains inside 892-917 is only the main page's. Wikidata Q1311990 is shared with grand-principality-of-serbia (and the Cliopatria row 'Serbia'): the Vlastimirovic principality (780-960) and the Vukanovic/Nemanjic Grand Principality (1094-1168) are different states 130 years apart with different dynasties, centres and a Byzantine interval (c. 971-1018 and after); they are kept as two dossiers. Gap 924-932: no Serbian state (Bulgarian annexation); the Bulgarian Cliopatria row covers the land from 926. Hungarian suzerainty? none. Byzantine nominal overlordship of Vlastimir ended with Theophilos's death in 842 (Vlastimir page) and Caslav accepted Byzantine overlordship under Romanos I (undated): not written as vassal events, the suzerain's side belongs in byzantine-empire. Gazetteer names needed: Zahumlje (alias of Herzegovina exists), Travunia, Pagania (Narentines), Destinikon, Bosna valley. The 961 Cliopatria sliver is marked wrong. The end year 960 follows the infobox; the body's c. 969-971 is recorded in the dissolve note.
